claims.quote: Loss of function mutations of the WW domain-containing oxidoreductase (WWOX) gene are associated with severe and fatal drug-resistant pediatric epileptic encephalopathy.

claims.object_text: mouse model of neuronal Wwox-deletion that exhibit spontaneous seizures
claims.quote: Using a mouse model of neuronal Wwox-deletion that exhibit spontaneous seizures,

claims.object_text: spontaneous bursting activity in the neocortex (network hyperexcitability)
claims.quote: identified spontaneous bursting activity in the neocortex, a marker of the underlying network hyperexcitability.

claims.object_text: increased phase-amplitude coupling and propagation from layer II/III to layer V
claims.quote: Spectral analysis of the neocortical bursting events highlighted increased phase-amplitude coupling, and a propagation from layer II/III to layer V.

claims.object_text: bursts were NMDAR and gap junction dependent
claims.quote: These bursts were NMDAR and gap junction dependent.

claims.object_text: elevated amplitude of excitatory post-synaptic currents in layer II/III pyramidal neurons
claims.quote: In layer II/III pyramidal neurons, Wwox knockout mice demonstrated elevated amplitude of excitatory post-synaptic currents,

claims.object_text: reduced frequency and amplitude of inhibitory post-synaptic currents
claims.quote: whereas the frequency and amplitude of inhibitory post-synaptic currents were reduced, as compared to heterozygote and wild-type littermate controls.

claims.object_text: neurons were depolarized with increased action potential frequency, sag current, and post-inhibitory rebound
claims.quote: Furthermore, these neurons were depolarized and demonstrated increased action potential frequency, sag current, and post-inhibitory rebound.

claims.object_text: plays an essential role in balancing neocortical excitability
